title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: AI found a flaw in 70% of the web
preheader: Governments pulled sites offline to patch it before hackers could strike.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Thursday, October 22, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: AI uncovers a flaw in PHP, taking websites offline worldwide
stories.why_important: Computer security firms used AI to find two critical flaws in PHP, a decades-old language that helps run about 70% of the world's websites. Governments and companies took sites offline to fix them before hackers could use the bugs.
stories.what_overlooked: No one has confirmed a hack yet, and the flaws went unnoticed for years. Attackers may have found them before this week's disclosure.
stories.prediction: Whether any hacked site appears in the next three days will show if criminals can use the flaws faster than companies fix them.

stories.story_title: Putin frees US prisoner and agrees to resume Ukraine talks
stories.why_important: Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff near St Petersburg and freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired American teacher convicted in Russia. The Kremlin said it is ready to restart three-way talks with Ukraine and the US next month, but Putin still rejected any truce.
stories.what_overlooked: Zelensky says Ukraine supports talks between negotiators by early November. Moscow named no date, and Putin dismissed any truce.
stories.prediction: Whether Moscow names a date and place for talks between negotiators within 72 hours will show if the promised restart is real.
